title: Stale session credit allocation after proxy rebind causes customer billing mismatches
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Several enterprise customers reported discrepancies where credits from short-lived sessions were being attributed to other tenants after a proxy rebind during traffic rebalancing. The issue appears when a tenant's long-lived session token is re-bound to a new proxy worker that simultaneously runs a background session cleanup job. A race allows stale session accounting rows to be picked up and attributed to an active tenant ID in the new worker process, resulting in unexpected positive or negative credit adjustments on customer ledgers.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a two-tenant host with proxy multiplexing enabled and short session caching (ttl=30s).
Create a long-lived session for tenant A and a short-lived burst session for tenant B.
Trigger a proxy rebind (simulated by restarting the proxy worker) while a background session compaction runs concurrently.
Observe ledger events emitted: session_end events for tenant B are sometimes written with tenant_id=A due to a stale local cache mapping in the rebinding worker.
Query billing_export and ledger tables to verify misattributed credit lines.
impact_summary: Misattributed credits lead to 1) inflated positive credits for some tenants, 2) sudden negative adjustments (billing spikes) for others, and 3) accounting noise requiring manual reconciliation. Two enterprise customers escalated to SEs with revenue-impacting invoices for the prior billing cycle.
priority_rationale: P0 due to direct customer revenue impact and active escalations requiring hotfix and reconciliation guidance.
mitigations: Applied temporary guard: proxy rebinding now fences session compaction jobs on the new worker for 60s after takeover to avoid picking up stale in-memory mappings (deploy staged 2026-02-26).
Added a read-verify on tenant_id for ledger writes; mismatches are now dropped to a quarantined queue for human review instead of being applied (hotfix PR #7891).
Notified impacted customers with proposed credit adjustments and a manual recon plan; transactions for Feb 22-25 were flagged for ledger review.
timeline: 2026-02-25: Customer A opened escalation via SE: unexplained +1200 credit line on Feb 23 invoice (SE ticket #SE-1189).
2026-02-25: Pager alerted on abnormal ledger write rate from proxy-rebind path; on-call started triage (Miguel).
2026-02-26: Reproduced locally following steps in steps_to_reproduce; confirmed tenant_id mismatch during worker takeover. Added initial mitigation to fence compaction jobs (deployed to staging).
2026-02-27: Hotfix PR #7891 created (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7891) implementing write-verify and quarantining logic; deployed to canary cluster (hosted-us-west-2).

2026-02-28: Canary monitoring: queued quarantined events stabilized at ~0.3% of prior miswrites; no new customer-visible misattributes observed. Cost dashboard link: https://dashboards.internal.redwood/billing/ledger-miswrites?range=7d

2026-03-01: SEs issued customer communications including temporary credit reversal proposals and the timeline for automated reconciliation. Two customers requested manual statements; CS and Finance engaged.

2026-03-03: Root cause analysis shows race between proxy rebind path and in-memory session-to-tenant cache invalidation; design doc created for durable tenant mapping and remote authoritative lookup (doc link: https://confluence.redwood/ENG/439213).

2026-03-05: Engineering to implement authoritative mapping with atomic compare-and-swap on ledger writes and add stricter provenance headers for session events; plan to include regression tests and e2e billing-sim harness (ETA: 2026-03-12).
acceptance_criteria: Automated e2e reproducer fails to produce any tenant_id misattributions in 10,000 simulated rebind+compaction cycles.
Canary release shows <0.01% quarantined ledger events for 72h and no new customer escalations related to this path.
Finance signoff on automated reconciliation patch that will apply corrective credit/debit adjustments with audit trail.
Postmortem published with timeline, root cause, and prevention actions.
next_steps: Implement authoritative tenant mapping service and replace local in-memory lookup in proxy workers (owner: Miguel).
Add atomic CAS on ledger write path and provenance fields (owner: Payments infra).
Expand e2e billing simulation harness to cover proxy-rebind scenarios and include it in CI (owner: Platform QE).
Prepare reconciliation runbook and automated correction job for flagged transactions (owner: Finance + Eng).
Draft postmortem and schedule customer follow-ups after reconciliation complete (owner: Aisha).
notes: This ticket captures the immediate mitigation and the delivery plan for a durable fix. Separate Finance tickets will own the reconciliation ledger runs and communications. Coordinate closely with Security if CAS or KMS changes are needed when modifying provenance headers.
